name: flecs
desc: Fast entity component system for C & C++
why: An entity component system library is a plumbing-adjacent tool, but it opens a door into simulation architecture worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: Flecs is a fast, lightweight Entity Component System library for C and C++, aimed at games and simulations with very large numbers of entities. You define components as plain data types, attach them to entities, and write systems (functions) that run over every entity matching a query. It is a library you compile into your program, not a standalone tool: the input is your C or C++ code, and the output is the running simulation loop, which the README drives with ecs_progress. It also has a web-based Flecs Explorer for monitoring and controlling a running app.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames ECS as a way to organize code and data so that games are 'larger, more complex and are easier to extend', and presents Flecs as a fast, portable implementation of that pattern.
brief.how_it_works: Entities are identifiers, components are datatypes added to entities, and systems are functions that run for all entities matching a component query. Storage is described as cache-friendly archetype/SoA, which the README says can process millions of entities every frame. Systems run inside a pipeline via ecs_progress, and the README mentions a lockless scheduler for running work across CPU cores.
brief.install_notes: The README I read contains no installation instructions, build commands, or package-manager lines, so I could not confirm anything beyond the Homebrew formula's existence. The README does say the C99 API is zero dependency and that the code base builds in less than 5 seconds. Language bindings for C#, Rust, Zig, Lua and Clojure are community-maintained and may lag master. Documentation is at the Flecs docs site, which I did not fetch.
brief.standout: The README claims it is the first open source ECS with full support for entity relationships, and it bundles a reflection framework with a JSON serializer, a statistics addon, and a browser-based explorer for live inspection. The same library runs in the browser through emscripten at flecs.dev/city, and the README lists a sizable set of shipped commercial games built on it.
brief.status: Appears maintained. The README has a live version badge pointing to GitHub releases and a CI badge for the master branch, and it says CI runs more than 13000 tests. I did not see a release date or last-commit date in what I fetched, so the exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: The homepage at https://www.flecs.dev returned almost no content (only the page title 'Flecs'), so the README was my main source. The brew description calls it a C and C++ library, and the README's main examples are C99 and C++17, so it is a programming-library entry rather than a command-line tool; there is nothing to run from a shell. The README's license badge says MIT but I did not read the LICENSE file. Community language bindings may not track master. The README's 'first open source ECS with full support for Entity Relationships' is the author's own claim, not something I verified.
quotes: Flecs is a fast and lightweight Entity Component System that lets you build games and simulations with millions of entities
Code base that builds in less than 5 seconds
Runs in the browser without modifications with emscripten
ECS is a way of organizing code and data that lets you build games that are larger, more complex and are easier to extend.
